provenance_note: All client, vendor, and human-contact data excluded at extraction. Only technical signage knowledge retained.

knowledge.plain_language_summary: A double-sided, internally lit monument built from two stacked aluminum cabinets. The brand and logo live in the upper cabinet, the tagline and web address in the lower one. Both cabinets light evenly from within through translucent faces, and a faux-brick base ties the sign visually to the building behind it.
knowledge.rationale: Stacking two separate cabinets with a reveal between them lets each message group light and update independently, and makes the lower cabinet a clean candidate for a future digital panel swap without rebuilding the whole sign.
knowledge.tradeoffs: An extruded-aluminum cabinet with translucent faces gives bright, even night presence and easy face service, but costs more than a flat non-illuminated panel and requires a power run and structural footing.
knowledge.when_to_use: Strong fit where a freestanding road-facing brand statement is needed at a site with vehicle traffic and night visibility requirements.

rules_observations: Two-cabinet split with a reveal maintains clear message grouping and legibility hierarchy.
Single internal-LED color temperature (5500K) across both cabinets keeps night color consistent.
craft_observations: Lead Pipe gray on topper and reveal frames a satin black body, giving a layered architectural read instead of a single flat slab.
Accent color is restricted to logo and url bar so it carries night pop without competing with itself.

aesthetic_notes.note: Faux brick base ties the sign to the masonry vernacular of the site, reading as part of the architecture rather than a stuck-on pole sign.
